questions.stem: Which sense do you use your nose for?
questions.explanation: We smell with our nose. We see with our eyes, hear with our ears and taste with our tongue.

questions.stem: Match each sense to what it tells us about the world.
pairs: hot or cold, rough or smooth
questions.explanation: Sight tells us colour and shape. Hearing tells us about sounds. Smell tells us about smells, taste about flavours, and touch about hot, cold and rough things.

questions.stem: Match each body part to the sense it gives us.
questions.explanation: Eyes give us sight, ears give us hearing, the nose gives us smell, the tongue gives us taste and the skin (hand) gives us touch.

questions.stem: Which of these is a light source?
questions.explanation: The Sun gives out its own light, so it is a light source. The Moon only reflects sunlight, and a notebook gives out no light.

questions.stem: Sort the pictures into things that give out light and things that make sound.
questions.explanation: The Sun, a torch, a candle and a light bulb give out light. A drum, a bell and a loudspeaker make sound.

questions.stem: Taller waves mean a louder sound, and waves that are close together mean a higher sound. Which picture shows a quiet, low sound?
questions.image_alt: Four wave drawings lettered A to D. Some waves are tall and some are short; some are close together and some are far apart.
questions.explanation: B has short waves, so the sound is quiet, and the waves are far apart, so the sound is low. A is loud and low, C is loud and high, and D is quiet and high.

questions.stem: Look at the picture. Why is there a dark shape on the screen?
questions.image_alt: A torch shining on an object, with a dark shadow shape on a screen behind the object.
options: The screen is made of dark paper.
The torch is too far away.
questions.explanation: A shadow is a dark shape made when something blocks the light. The object is in the way of the light from the torch.

questions.stem: Which of these give out their own light? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: The Sun, a candle and a torch make their own light. The Moon and a mirror only reflect light that comes from somewhere else.

questions.stem: A ___ is a dark shape made when something blocks the light.
questions.explanation: When an object blocks light, it makes a shadow on the other side.

questions.stem: A drum, a bell and your voice are all sound ___.
questions.explanation: Anything that makes a sound is a sound source. A drum, a bell, a bird and your voice are all sound sources.

questions.stem: We can see things in a completely dark room.
questions.explanation: We need light to see. With no light, no light enters our eyes, so we cannot see anything.

questions.stem: The Moon is a light source because it gives out its own light.
questions.explanation: The Moon does not make light. It looks bright because it reflects light from the Sun.

questions.stem: What can you find out with your skin by touching? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Your skin (touch) can feel hot or cold, rough or smooth, and hard or soft. Sweet or sour is for the tongue, and loud or quiet is for the ears.

questions.stem: Which sense tells us each of these things? Sort the words.
questions.explanation: We use sight for bright and dark, hearing for loud and quiet, taste for sweet and sour, and touch for rough and smooth.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to show how your senses keep you safe.
sequence: There is smoke from a fire.
Your nose sends a message to your brain.
Your brain tells you something is wrong.
You get out and tell an adult.
questions.explanation: Your senses send messages to your brain. The brain tells you what is happening, and you can then act to stay safe.

questions.stem: Why can't you see anything in a dark room with no light?
questions.model_answer: We need light to see. With no light, no light enters our eyes.
questions.explanation: We need light to see. In a room with no light, no light reaches our eyes, so we cannot see.

questions.stem: Which pair of words describes sounds?
questions.explanation: Sounds can be loud or quiet. Hot and cold, and rough and smooth, describe things we touch, and sweet and sour describe tastes.

questions.stem: Mina smells smoke coming from the kitchen at home. What should she do?
options: Go close to look at the fire.
questions.explanation: A smell of smoke can mean a fire. The safe thing is to tell an adult at once and keep away from the smoke.

questions.stem: Imran is crossing a village road when he hears a loud car horn behind him. What is the safest thing to do?
options: Cover his ears and stay in the road.
Stop and look for the vehicle.
Close his eyes and keep walking.
questions.explanation: A horn is a warning sound. The safe choice is to stop and look to see where the vehicle is before moving.

questions.stem: Sumi opens the milk at breakfast. It smells bad and tastes sour. What should she do?
options: Add sugar and drink it anyway.
Put it back in the fridge.
Drink it quickly before it gets worse.
Pour it away and tell her mother.
questions.explanation: Milk that smells bad and tastes sour has gone off. Our senses warn us, so we should not drink it, and we should tell an adult.

questions.stem: Raju cannot see. He reads Braille with his fingers and knows his friends by their voices. This shows that we can learn about the world with our other senses.
questions.explanation: Touch and hearing give Raju a lot of information. Our senses work as a team, and when one sense is missing, the others help.

questions.stem: How can classmates help Raju at school? Choose all that are right.
options: move his things without telling him
questions.explanation: Raju uses a cane to feel the path and listens to sounds. Classmates can keep bags off the floor, tell him when things move and guide him kindly.

questions.stem: In a touch test, the children closed their eyes before feeling each object. Why?
options: So the teacher could not see the objects.
Because touch only works with eyes closed.
So they used only touch, not sight.
Because eyes can feel objects too.
questions.explanation: Closing their eyes meant they used only the sense of touch, so they could not use sight to decide. It made the test fair.

questions.stem: Joy says, 'The Moon is a light source because it shines at night.' What is the best reply?
options: The Moon makes its own light, like a candle.
We cannot really see the Moon at night.
The Moon is bright, so it is a light source.
The Moon only reflects light from the Sun.
questions.explanation: The Moon looks bright because sunlight bounces off it. It does not make its own light, so it is not a light source.

questions.stem: Give two examples of how your senses can keep you safe.
questions.model_answer: I smell smoke and know there may be a fire. I hear a car horn and stop. I feel something hot and pull my hand away.
questions.explanation: Smell warns us of smoke, hearing warns us of a car horn, touch warns us of something hot, and taste tells us that milk has gone sour.

questions.stem: Taller waves mean a louder sound, and waves that are close together mean a higher sound. Which picture shows a loud, high sound, like a loud whistle?
questions.image_alt: Four wave drawings lettered A to D. Some waves are tall and some are short; some are close together and some are far apart.
questions.explanation: C has tall waves, so it is loud, and the waves are close together, so it is high. A is loud and low, B is quiet and low, and D is quiet and high.
